stem: A manufacturing study measures defect rate across 3 factorys, each containing multiple production lines. factory A has 15 observations with mean 70.6 % (within-factory SD = 9.7). factory B has 8 observations with mean 77.8 % (within-factory SD = 3.6). factory C has 8 observations with mean 58.4 % (within-factory SD = 6.0). The between-factory standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 3.1 and 7.8 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true defect rate for factory C, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-factory variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for factory C: 60.0 % (shrunk from raw 58.4). Range [59.2, 61.9] as between-factory SD varies from 3.1 to 7.8. Pooled mean: 69.3.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 69.3 % (weighted average of 3 factory means).
Shrinkage factor for factory C: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=5.2: B = 0.857.
Interval [59.2, 61.9] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (58.4) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (69.3) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
